html:
SMTO-CMP-0047 — SMTO stopped after it couldn't confirm the task was finished

GUID: 68561fe2-8c73-4f92-bb98-bff336d3443d
Slug: completion-convergence-limit
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • SMTO tried three times to mark the task as done, but each time it couldn't show that everything you asked for was finished. It stopped as Partial; the work and results so far are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the task's final message. It lists the parts of your request that SMTO could not confirm. Those listed parts are what stopped the task from being marked done.
  2. Send a message asking SMTO to check or finish just those parts, and add any detail it needs, such as the exact result you expect. SMTO stopped because it kept repeating the same claim; a focused request gives it something new and specific to do.
  3. Don't ask SMTO to redo the whole task. Work that already succeeded is kept, and repeating it could make the same changes again.

What success looks like

  • The task ends as Completed and its answer covers the parts that were listed as unconfirmed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the task's final message, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Bound completion corrections in Agent Checks as a fix; it only lets SMTO repeat the same rejected claim more times.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run stopped as partial because the completion retry bound was reached after three rejected completion declarations without a relevant state change.

What this means

  • Completion convergence reuses an equivalent rejected declaration at the same evidence revision, and the enabled retry bound stops after three rejections without relevant state change. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Completion convergence reuses an equivalent rejected declaration at the same evidence revision, and the enabled retry bound stops after three rejections without relevant state change.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect new_evidence_required and the concrete rejection; a corrected optional declaration can succeed without new tool work.

How to fix it

  • Inspect completion_feedback and completion_unmet_details in the run state, or the unmet items listed in the final response, to see the concrete rejection and whether new_evidence_required is set. Re-prompt or resume with a corrected declaration or the genuinely missing evidence; keep protocol.completion_retry_bound ('Bound completion corrections') enabled and do not repeat completed work.
  • Correct the specific declaration or obtain genuinely required evidence, preserving existing receipts and avoiding repeated unchanged claims.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A corrected declaration or relevant new evidence satisfies the real unmet condition.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat completed work to repair this diagnostic or declaration.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
